text_en: Can follow speech that is very slow and carefully articulated, with long pauses to take in the meaning.
Can pick out concrete information such as names, places and times in a short, slow, clearly spoken exchange on a familiar everyday topic.
source_note: Understanding conversation between other people, A1, and Overall oral comprehension, A1.

text_en: Can understand numbers, prices and times given slowly and clearly.
source_note: Listening to announcements and instructions, A1.

text_en: Can understand very short, simple texts one phrase at a time, picking up familiar names, words and basic phrases and rereading as needed.
Can understand short, simple messages on postcards and in simple personal emails.
Can recognise familiar names, words and very basic phrases on simple notices in the most common everyday situations.
Can produce simple, mainly isolated phrases about people and places.
Can describe themselves, what they do and where they live.
Can ask and answer simple questions and respond to simple statements on very familiar topics or in areas of immediate need.
Can introduce themselves and use basic greeting and leave taking expressions.
Can ask and answer questions about themselves and other people: where they live, people they know, things they have.
Can write simple isolated phrases and sentences about themselves.
Can fill in a simple form with personal details: name, nationality, address, age, date of birth.
Uses the personal pronouns with sein and haben in the present tense.
source_note: A1 grammar inventory. Row A1.1 of the German grammar sequence in docs/05.

text_en: Uses the present tense endings of regular verbs such as wohnen, kommen and heissen with the correct pronoun.
source_note: A1 grammar inventory. Row A1.2 of the German grammar sequence in docs/05.

text_en: Forms statements, yes or no questions and W questions with the verb in the correct position.
source_note: A1 grammar inventory. Row A1.3 of the German grammar sequence in docs/05.

text_en: Uses the definite article der, die, das with the gender of common nouns in the nominative.
source_note: A1 grammar inventory. Row A1.4 of the German grammar sequence in docs/05.

text_en: Uses greetings and farewells and the words needed to give and ask for a name, a country and a city.
source_note: Thematic list: Persönliche Angaben, Begrüßung und Abschied.

text_en: Understands and says the cardinal numbers one to ten and uses them for telephone numbers and house numbers.
source_note: Thematic list: Zahlen. Row A1.12 of the sequence in docs/05 covers numbers, dates and the clock.
